assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: full; driver_capability: ready

## Reasoning

The scenario asserts one user-observable arc — `ready → working → ready` with at least one tool call mid-turn, and the negative invariant that state NEVER enters `waiting`.

**agent_supports: yes.** GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.77 executes shell tool calls inside a turn: `tool.execution_start` / `tool.execution_complete` pairs (on `data.toolCallId`) were observed live in `$COPILOT_HOME/session-state/<session-id>/events.jsonl`, with `bash` as the tool name. `--allow-all` pre-approves tools, so a safe `echo hello` runs with no confirmation prompt and therefore emits no `permission.requested` — the ungated path this cell is about. (`--allow-all-tools` alone is NOT sufficient: a subagent's bash still hit denied-no-approval-rule; the driver uses `--allow-all`.)

**daemon_capability: full.** Every event the arc needs is one the copilot parser already maps (`core/adapters/inbound/agents/copilot/parser.go`):

| observable | events.jsonl event | parser output |
|---|---|---|
| turn opens (`ready→working`) | `user.message` | `user_message` |
| tool call runs mid-turn | `tool.execution_start` / `tool.execution_complete` | `function_call` / `function_call_output`, paired on `toolCallId` |
| turn ends (`working→ready`) | `assistant.turn_end` | `turn_done` |
| the negative invariant | `permission.requested` — NOT emitted under `--allow-all` | `permission_requested` (the only route to `waiting`) |

The tool round-trip keeps the session `working` rather than settling it: `parseAssistantMessage` deliberately never ends the turn (only `assistant.turn_end` does), and `session.start` / model-change / usage / shutdown events are all `Skip=true` so no bookkeeping line can flip a finished session back to `working`. `waiting` is reachable ONLY through `permission_requested`, so with no gate the invariant holds structurally, not by luck.

Birth is the PRESESSION shape, not single-birth. Copilot creates the session directory at launch but writes `events.jsonl` only when the first prompt is sent (driver SEAM 3), so at launch the file watcher has nothing and `processlifecycle`'s scanner emits a `proc-<PID>` row (scanner.go:347), which is superseded when the real transcript appears under a DIFFERENT session id (`sessionIDFromPath` = the directory name). The spec therefore models the birth as two phases and anchors every later phase to `session_birth`, templated from the mistral-vibe sibling (same `FilesUnderRoot` + dir-keyed id shape).

PID binding is by cwd (`DiscoverPIDByCWD("copilot", …)`, pid.go) against the `ExactName{copilot}` matcher; the driver launches under tmux with `-c $RUN_CWD` canonicalized, so the match is exact.

**driver_capability: ready.** The recipe needs `send` / `wait_turn` / `sleep` only; all three are in the driver's `DRIVE_ELICITS` and genuinely ported — `wait_turn` counts `"type":"assistant.turn_end"` occurrences, an EXACT completed-turn count rather than the tail-quietness heuristic other drivers settle for. No `keys`, `reset_session` or `restart` is involved, so none of the stubbed arms is touched.

## Observations

`cost_nonzero` + `tokens_nonzero` are asserted and are derivable OFFLINE from the staged transcript alone — unlike mistral-vibe/kiro-cli, whose usage lives in a sidecar. Output tokens land per `assistant.message.outputTokens` while the session runs (`queueOutputIncrement`), and both models this account can reach are priced in the replay capacity snapshot (`gpt-5-mini` directly; `claude-haiku-4.5` via the alias added for #1256).

`model` is deliberately NOT pinned: `--model` accepts only `auto` on this account and the router picks per turn between `gpt-5-mini` and `claude-haiku-4.5` (both seen in ONE live 1.0.77 session), so an exact-match assertion would fail on router choice, not on a regression. `record` fills it from the recording.
caveats: The no-waiting invariant rests entirely on the driver's `--allow-all` flag: without it Copilot raises `permission.requested`, the parser emits `permission_requested`, and the session correctly enters `waiting` — which is the SIBLING gated-tool scenario, not a failure of this one. If a recording ever flips to waiting here, tighten the launch flags rather than weakening the spec.

`events.jsonl` does not exist until the first prompt is sent (driver SEAM 3, live-verified on 1.0.77), so the real session is born `ready` and moves to `working` within roughly the same second. The `session_birth` state observation is therefore tight and could be coalesced with `turn_start` by the tailer's debounce; if `record` sees it collapsed, re-anchor the phases rather than dropping the ready birth.

PROVISIONAL on emission: daemon=full is derived from reading the parser plus the live-captured 1.0.77 envelope fixtures in metrics_test.go, not from a recording of THIS scenario. The tool-pair and turn-boundary events were confirmed live (irrlicht's has_open_tool_call went true on tool.execution_start and false on tool.execution_complete); the end-to-end arc is composition and `record` is what settles it.

Input tokens are only reported at `session.shutdown` (a `session.usage_checkpoint` carries `totalNanoAiu` but NO token counts — verified live on 1.0.77). This recipe has no `exit_clean` step, so the recording will carry output tokens only. That still satisfies tokens_nonzero/cost_nonzero, but the input half of the summary will read 0.

Recording spends real Copilot AI credits. Export `COPILOT_AVAILABLE_TOOLS=bash` before driving (the driver honours it and passes `--available-tools=bash`): tool definitions are ~8.3k of ~12k input tokens per turn, so restricting to the one tool this scenario needs roughly halves per-turn cost.

sources.note: tool.execution_start/complete → function_call/function_call_output paired on toolCallId; assistant.turn_end → turn_done; permission.requested → permission_requested is the ONLY route to waiting; lifecycle/usage events are Skip
Source is FilesUnderRoot over ~/.copilot/session-state with sessionIDFromPath = the <session-id> directory (transcript basename is the constant events.jsonl); ExactName{copilot} matcher
DiscoverPIDByCWD("copilot", cwd, …) — cwd-only binding, no sidecar fallback; grounds the pid_bind phase
maybeTrackNewPID emits sessionID proc-<pid> (line 347) when no active transcript covers the PID, superseded once the real transcript appears — the presession two-phase birth this spec models

DRIVE_ELICITS carries send/wait_turn/sleep; launches with --allow-all and honours COPILOT_AVAILABLE_TOOLS; turn_count greps assistant.turn_end for an exact turn count; SEAM 3 records that events.jsonl appears only at the first prompt

live-captured 1.0.77 envelope fixtures: assistant.message.outputTokens is the live token signal; modelMetrics/currentTokens exist only on session.shutdown; both gpt-5-mini and claude-haiku-4.5 appear in one session
TestCopilotAlias_ResolvesToRealCostEstimate — claude-haiku-4.5 prices non-zero via the #1256 alias; gpt-5-mini already priced on its own
both gpt-5-mini and claude-haiku-4-5 carry pricing in the committed replay snapshot, so cost_nonzero is satisfiable in the OFFLINE golden
presession-shaped sibling for the same scenario (FilesUnderRoot + dir-keyed session id) — the two-phase birth templated here

preconditions: copilot CLI 1.0.77 on PATH and authenticated (credentials live in the OS keychain, so COPILOT_HOME isolation needs no re-login)
An active Copilot plan with AI credits — this recording spends them
irrlichd is recording (run-cell.sh isolated mode, or --attach against a --record daemon)
tmux available (the interactive driver drives the REPL through it)
setup: The driver isolates state under $STAGING/copilot-home via COPILOT_HOME (the supported lever; --config-dir is deprecated) and seeds trustedFolders + askedSetupTerminals so neither first-run prompt blocks the input box

Launch is `copilot --allow-all --no-color` in a fresh per-run cwd under <staging>/cwd/, so the bash call auto-executes and no permission.requested is ever written — that is what makes the no-waiting invariant structural rather than incidental

Recommended: export COPILOT_AVAILABLE_TOOLS=bash before driving. The driver forwards it as --available-tools=bash, which drops the unused tool definitions (~8.3k of ~12k input tokens) and roughly halves the credits this cell costs
Interactive, not headless: the REPL must outlive the turn so the daemon observes the working→ready settle rather than a process exit
wait_turn counts assistant.turn_end lines — Copilot writes an explicit turn boundary, so the wait is exact

script.text: Run the shell command `echo hello` with the bash tool, then reply with just: done

verify: events.jsonl shows a transient proc-<PID> presession born ready, then the real <session-id> session (a DIFFERENT id, the session-state directory name) born ready when the transcript appears
events.jsonl shows exactly one ready→working and one working→ready transition for the real session
at least one tool_use for the bash tool falls inside that working span (tool.execution_start / tool.execution_complete paired on toolCallId)
events.jsonl contains NO state_transition to waiting for any session during the run (--allow-all → no permission.requested)
the newest recording's replay summary shows cum_output_tokens > 0 and estimated_cost_usd > 0, with model_name one of gpt-5-mini / claude-haiku-4.5 (router's choice — not pinned)
